back: The route a product takes from producer to final customer, including any intermediaries.
A business that buys in bulk from producers, stores goods and sells smaller quantities to retailers.
A person or business that sells for a producer in return for a commission and does not own the goods.
Direct to consumer; producer to retailer; producer to wholesaler to retailer; through an agent; e-commerce.
The product, the market, cost, control, competitors, and location and infrastructure.
Perishable goods need short, fast channels so that they reach customers while fresh.
Each intermediary adds a mark-up, so longer chains usually raise the customer's price, but save the producer cost and effort.
Transport, storage and handling of goods, including warehouses, packing, delivery and keeping shelves stocked. Digital products can be delivered electronically.
